newsitem.title: FINLAND: Summit may discuss Middle East, Russia says.
newsitem.headline: Summit may discuss Middle East, Russia says.

text.p: Presidents Bill Clinton and Boris Yeltsin may discuss the crisis in the Middle East peace process at their summit in Helsinki, Russian presidential press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky said on Thursday.
"If there is time, the presidents may exchange opinions on these problems. At least the Russian delegation is ready for this," Yastrzhembsky told reporters in the Finnish capital.
Israeli troops fired teargas at hundreds of stone-throwing Palestinians protesting against Israel's building of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on Thursday.
Aides to Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat denounced Israel's offer to finish making peace in six months as a trick and publicity stunt aimed at scrapping existing accords and dodging world criticism.

In Helsinki, Yastrzhembsky gave no details but said Moscow wanted to play a bigger role in the Middle East peace process, where it enjoyed good ties with some Arab countries in Soviet times and is now developing relations with Israel.
Russia and the United States are co-sponsors of the peace process but Moscow has played a secondary role to Washington.
Both Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have visited Moscow in recent weeks as Russia sought to raise its profile in the region.
"In the past Russia's role was rather formal. Now we have certain chances which the United States does not have in the Middle East," Yastrzhembsky said.
"Many of our traditional partners support a bigger role for Russia in this region."
